hook: SCP-645 is a marble face modelled on the Bocca della Verità carving in Rome, and just as the legend promises, it bites off the hand of anyone who lies with their hand inside its mouth. Almost the entire article is one test that goes off the rails because the D-class subject already knows the story. The transcript is profane, contains a confession to murder and ends with someone losing a hand.
whyItMatters:
It takes a real legend and simply lets it be literally true, then uses that to ask what counts as honesty. The comedy comes from a terrified man phrasing every sentence so carefully that nothing he says could possibly be false.

The page is tagged as a rewrite, and the closing request to move it from Safe to Euclid shows how one incident can change the Foundation's whole picture of an object.
thingsToNotice:
D-45951 dodges each scripted lie by framing it as something the researchers are making him say, and simple questions about his name or a prime number spiral into hedges and corrections. The mood turns when Rensburg presses him about his convictions: he first pleads self-defence, then admits he killed the witnesses because he enjoys it, and the carving spits his hand out and will not take it back.

The sting arrives afterwards, when Rensburg casually admits he never knew the details of those crimes and was bluffing. The mouth stretches open and shoots a frog-like tongue across the room, severing his right hand and breaking Long's shoulder on the way back. The site director concludes the carving is probably sapient and acted out of resentment at the deception, while a footnote quietly names the film the subject had seen as Roman Holiday.
